If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: I doubt the restart caused that, but let's check it out — Airplane Mode would definitely explain the missing signal bars. Let me take a look at your network status.

It looks like I'm not able to run the remote device diagnostics on your line right now, so I can't check or toggle Airplane Mode from my side.

Based on what you've described — the Airplane Mode icon is showing with no signal bars — Airplane Mode is ON, and that would fully explain the "No Service" you're seeing, independent of the suspension we just cleared. A restart wouldn't normally enable it, but it can be toggled accidentally (for example from the quick-settings panel).

**Please try this on your phone:**
1. Swipe down from the top of the screen to open the quick settings panel.
2. Tap the **Airplane Mode / ✈️** tile so it turns **off**.
3. Wait a few seconds and check whether the signal bars return.

Let me know what the status bar shows after that. If the signal comes back, you're all set. If it still shows no service with Airplane Mode off, tell me and I'll take it from there.

turns.thought: I understand the frustration — let's keep going. Let me try running a couple of checks on your device.

I'm sorry this is dragging on — and I want to be upfront with you: my remote diagnostic tools for your device aren't responding right now, so I can't check your SIM status or the underlying network settings myself.

Here's the good news: I confirmed on the account side that your line **555-123-2002** is **Active**, with no suspension and a valid contract through 2026-12-31. So this is very likely a device-side setting, not an account problem.

Two things to try on the phone:

**1. Turn mobile data back on**
Your status bar shows "Data Disabled." Go to **Settings → Network & Internet / Connections → Mobile Network** and switch **Mobile Data** to ON.

**2. Reseat the SIM card**
Still no bars after that? Power the phone off, eject the SIM tray, make sure the SIM is lying flat and seated properly, reinsert it firmly, then power back on. A SIM that isn't making good contact is a common cause of a persistent "No Signal" with an otherwise healthy line.

If you try both and it's still showing no signal, tell me and I'll get you over to a human agent in technical support, who can run the deeper device diagnostics with you. Also worth noting: if it does turn out to be a damaged SIM, that's something they'll need to handle — a replacement or security-related SIM issue isn't something I can resolve from here.
turns.execution_output: User: I can only do one thing at a time here — could you tell me which one to try first? Should I turn mobile data back on, or go ahead and reseat the SIM card?

turns.thought:
Good question — let's do **the SIM card reseat first.**

Here's why: mobile data being switched off wouldn't make your signal bars disappear. You'd normally still see bars (and be able to make calls) with data off. The fact that you're seeing **"No Signal"** at all means the phone isn't talking to the network in the first place — and a SIM that isn't making solid contact is the most common reason for that on an otherwise healthy line. It's also the step most likely to actually fix it, rather than just clearing one symptom.

**How to reseat it:**
1. Power the phone **off** completely.
2. Use the SIM eject tool (or a small paperclip) to pop open the SIM tray.
3. Take the SIM card out, check it's clean and not damaged, then lay it back in the tray **flat and seated properly**.
4. Push the tray firmly back in until it's flush.
5. Power the phone back on and give it a minute or two to register on the network.

Once it's back up, check the status bar. If the bars come back, then go ahead and switch **Mobile Data** to ON — that takes care of the "Data Disabled" part.

If you're still staring at "No Signal" after that, tell me and I'll get you transferred to technical support, who can run deeper diagnostics on the line and, if needed, sort out a SIM replacement — that's not something I can do from here.
